text:
Maria L.: ok team — we need a reproducible parity benchmark for model comparisons that removes runtime/kerneI/batching variability. not 'close enough'.
Tom H.: +1. what are the must-haves? exact tokenization, identical decode params, same stop sequences, and same input ordering right? :thinking_face: 
Arjun S.: yes. also KV cache warmup state must be deterministic. replay vs synthetic diverge a lot if KV handling differs.
Jen K.: draft checklist:
- canonical tokenizer (hf artifact id)
- fixed seed for sampling or deterministic decode (greedy/topk with seed)
- identical prompt trimming/normalization
- same batch shapes and padding policy
- same initial KV cache priming (or clear it)
- capture kernel selection hints (which kernels were used)
Tom H.: agree. add: record per-step kernel name + time, mem stats, and per-token latency histogram. keep raw traces.
Maria L.: proposing a harness config we can land:
```yaml
benchmark_name: parity-protocol-v1
runs: 5
models: ["loria-7b", "vicuna-13b-quant"]
seq_len: 1024
decode: {strategy: greedy, temp: 0.0}
tokenizer: "hf://redwood/tokenizers/parity-v1"
batch_policy: "fixed"
batch_sizes: [1,4,8]
kv_warm_steps: 0
align_tokenizer: true
log_kernel_selection: true
collect_traces: true
```
Arjun S.: one more: add a replay mode that forces the same token boundaries as the canonical tokenizer, even if the model's default differs. i.e. apply tokenizer to prompt first, then replay token ids.
Tom H.: sounds good. we should also run a synthetic traffic flow to stress batching heuristics: poisson arrival vs uniform. compare latency P50/P95 with same effective throughput.
perf-bot: quick summary from today's dry run (parity-protocol-v1):
- run id: 2026-03-15-01
- models: loria-7b, vicuna-13b-quant
- seq_len: 1024, batch: 4
- observed regression: vicuna-13b-quant P95 +18% vs baseline on node type g5.
- kernel switch detected at token 64 -> switched from fast_attn to fallback_matmul for that sequence length.
- KV cache miss-rate: 0.7% (replay harness), padding inefficiency: 12%
Dave R.: perf-bot — can you attach the kernel trace? i want the per-kernel op times.
perf-bot: attached: s3://redwood-ci/parity/2026-03-15-01/traces.tar.gz (contains per-token kernel map + nvtx)
Jen K.: initial hypothesis: quantized matmul kernel regression under certain sequence alignments + batching reorder. the kernel selector uses estimated cost; small change to the cost model could flip to fallback_matmul which is slower on our quantized paths.
Maria L.: action items:
- Arjun: add tokenizer-align pass to replay tool + verify tokenid parity across models (due EOD).
- Tom: run poisson vs uniform synthetic flows at 500, 1000 qps and capture P50/P95; log kernel selection for each.
- Jen: reproduce kernel selector flip in unit harness (isolate cost heuristic), open PR for new calibration.
- Dave: fetch trace, run per-op profiler and share hotspot list.
Tom H.: will do. using: `./harness run --cfg parity-protocol-v1.yaml --mode synthetic --pattern poisson --qps 1000`
Arjun S.: note: when you replay replays, use `--align-tokenizer` flag. command: `./harness replay --session s3://ci-replays/2026-03-01.parquet --align-tokenizer --seed 42`
Jen K.: if we confirm kernel flip is the root cause we should add a guard in the runtime: prefer fast_attn for quantized models up to 128 tokens unless mem > X. keep it small change first.
Maria L.: sounds good. please post short run notes in this thread when done. we want a clean apples-to-apples artifact for the release benchmark page (bench/benchmarking.md) and a pinned trace for reproducibility. :white_check_mark:
Tom H.: will report back in ~2 hours with the synthetic runs.
Arjun S.: started tokenizer parity job now, i'll ping when token ids match exactly across models.
Dave R.: grabbed traces, starting nvprof pass. expecting hotspot around `q_matmul` op on quant path.
perf-bot: CI note: parity-protocol-v1 jobs are non-blocking; failures open a perf issue: https://go.redwood/p/perf/1267
Maria L.: thanks all — keep notes concise here. once we converge we'll convert checklist into a CI job that must pass for apples parity.
